questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to become a synchronised swimmer
A new trend of swimming with a tail like a mermaid
The difference between aerobic and anaerobic exercise
questions.why: Neil talks about 'the new craze of mermaiding' and they hear from Emma Longden about it.

questions.q: How often does Neil go swimming?
questions.why: Neil says 'I try to get to the pool once a week and do a few lengths'.

options: He prefers going to the gym and lifting weights instead
He doesn't like getting wet and finds it boring
questions.why: Rob says 'I just don't like getting wet - and swimming up and down a pool is just boring!'

questions.q: Where did the idea of mermaiding start?
questions.why: Neil says 'The idea originated in America but is now popular in the UK and Europe.'

questions.q: According to Emma Longden, what do you need to do mermaiding?
options: A single fin like a tail on your feet
questions.why: She says 'Mermaiding is putting a monofin on your feet. Putting a beautiful tail on'.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a benefit of mermaiding that Emma mentions?
options: A workout for the whole body
questions.why: She mentions confidence, a whole body workout, balance and co-ordination, but not losing weight.

questions.q: What part of mermaiding does Rob like the sound of?
options: Being with other people and having fun
questions.why: Rob says 'I like the sound of the social aspect'.

questions.q: Why do many adults take mermaiding classes, according to Emma?
options: They want to learn so they can teach their own children to swim safely
They wanted to be mermaids as children and now can
questions.why: She says many adults 'want to live out their childhood dreams' of being a mermaid.
